habit_scope: Batter boards and string to hold building lines while the hole is dug. FM 5-426 Ch4 is the US habit (boards 3 or 4 ft outside, before excavation disturbs the corner stakes). CMHC Ch6 is a Canadian sequence note (offset marks; boards after excavation) — Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. 1–2 story wood SFR. Squaring: 6-8-10 and equal diagonals are variants inside this Method, not separate Methods.
how_it_is_done: FM 5-426 Ch4 LAYOUT: 'Layout prepares the site for the foundation.' Work from an established line such as a road or a property line parallel to construction. Establish the outer perimeter, then the frontage, then the four corners. Drive stakes at each corner. 'Dimensions are determined accurately during each step.'

Batter boards preserve the lines when the hole eats the corner stakes. FM: 'Batter boards are a temporary framework used to assist in locating corners when laying out a foundation. Batter-board posts are made from 2 x 4 or 4 x 4 material; corner stakes are made from 2 x 2s. Batter boards are made from 1 x 4 or 1 x 6 pieces.' 'Excavating for a foundation will disturb the stakes, so batter boards are set up outside the boundary established by the stakes to preserve definite and accurate building lines. Heavy cord or fine wire is stretched from one batter board to another to mark these lines.'

Location (FM Fig 4-3): 'Right-angle batter boards are erected 3 or 4 feet outside of each corner stake. Straight batter boards are erected 3 or 4 feet outside of the line stakes.' Tops at the exact height of the top of the foundation. Level with a carpenter's level. Framing square to get the right-angle boards close to perpendicular. 'Angle saw cuts may be made or nails driven into the tops of the boards to hold the lines in place. Separate cuts or nails may be used for the building line, the foundation line, the footing line, and excavation lines. These grooves permit the removal and replacement of the lines in the correct position.'

Extend lines over the corner stakes (FM Extending Lines). Where foundation walls are wide at the bottom, 'the excavation must be larger than the laid-out size. To lay out dimensions of this excavation, measure out as far as required from the building line on each batter board and stretch lines between these points, outside the first layout.' Plumb bob over the corner stakes to square the crossing lines. Check lines with a line level or a carpenter's level.

Square the layout. FM names two methods — variants inside this Method, not alts: (1) 6-8-10: measure 6 ft and 8 ft on the two lines, adjust until the diagonal is 10 ft. 'Multiples of 6-8-10 may be used for large layouts; for example, 12-16-20 for a layout 50 feet by 100 feet. For accuracy, never start with a measurement of less than 6 feet.' (2) Diagonal method: opposite-corner diagonals equal on a rectangle. Adjust until they match.

Irregular building: FM 'first lay out a large rectangle which will comprise the entire building or the greater part of it' then the remaining small rectangles, each proved separately. Not a separate Method.

CMHC Ch6 (Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC): offset markings before the hole because the first stakes will be lost; those marks are used AFTER excavation to erect batter boards (Fig 28, Fig 30). Three stakes of suitable length at each corner at least 1.2 m (4 ft) beyond the lines of the excavation; tops of all boards level and at the same elevation; wire or stout string on the outside edge of the foundation wall; saw kerfs 6 to 8 mm (1/4 to 3/8 in.) or nails. Squaring: equal diagonals, or triangulation in multiples of 300/400/500 mm (12/16/20 in.). Do not copy CMHC metric 3-4-5 as the US habit — US printed 6-8-10 is FM. The post-excavation board sequence is a Canadian note, not a second US Method.

CMHC Ch2: 'Arrange for access to the site and temporary power during this stage' (drawings/financing/permits). Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. Temp toilet is silent. Gap gap-P03-temp-toilet. Do not invent a toilet Method.
trades: FM: carpenter layout — no crew size. AF&PA names job foreman, subcontractors, building inspector. CMHC: land surveyor may be required (Ch2 Building Layout).
tools_equipment: FM 5-426 Ch4 named tools: string line; sledgehammer; posthole auger; handsaw; ax or hatchet; hammer; chalk line; 100-foot/30-meter tape; tracing tape (~1 in cotton, usually 200 ft); carpenter's level; line level (hang halfway between points); automatic level; 8d nails; plumbing bob; framing square.
inspection_hold_points: Four corners staked; batter boards 3 or 4 ft outside so the hole does not eat the lines (FM).
Lines square: 6-8-10 (never start under 6 ft) or equal diagonals (FM). CMHC equal diagonals / 12-16-20 in triangulation is Canadian — confirm AHJ; not IRC.
Separate saw cuts or nails for building / foundation / footing / excavation lines (FM).
Plumb bob over corner stakes; lines level (FM).
Layout complete before excavation proceeds (CMHC Ch2 Stages). Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC.
when_this_beats_habit: This is the habit. Books did not file a transit-only or GPS-only Method. 6-8-10 and diagonals are variants inside this Method.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Copying CMHC 24–28 in excavation width or 300-400-500 mm triangulation as US habit. Inventing a toilet Method. Layout that ignores the permit setbacks. Using FM wall/column foundation types from the same chapter as a P05 type swap — those are military/TO notes, not inland SFR habit.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They did — string and boards. What they skip is 3–4 ft outside so the bucket does not kill the lines, and proving square with 6-8-10 or diagonals before the hole.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
permit_gate_notes: Layout follows the permitted drawings and setbacks (CMHC Ch6: check municipality for minimum setback and side yard before deciding exact location). Confirm with AHJ. Not a stamp. Canadian setback language — confirm AHJ; not IRC.
risk_if_swapped_late: Moving corners after the hole is open is a reshoot and maybe a setback fail. Catch vs survey and permit set.
plain_language_summary: Put the house on the dirt with boards and string, not with a guess. Corner stakes first. Boards 3 or 4 feet outside so the excavator does not wipe the lines. Square it: 6-8-10 (never start under 6 feet) or equal diagonals. Separate marks for building, foundation, footing, and the hole. CMHC is Canadian — do not copy their millimetres as US habit. Toilet is a Gap.
spanish_summary: Ponga la casa en la tierra con tablas y piola, no a ojo. Estacas de esquina primero. Tablas a 3 o 4 pies afuera para que la pala no borre las líneas. Cuadre: 6-8-10 (nunca menos de 6 pies) o diagonales iguales. Marcas aparte para edificio, cimiento, zapata y hueco. CMHC es canadiense. El baño portátil es Gap.
locators: FM 5-426 Ch4 Layout; Laying Out a Rectangular Building Site; Setting Batter Boards; Extending Lines; Squaring Lines (6-8-10 and diagonal); Figs 4-1, 4-3, 4-4
CMHC Ch6 Placement of the House; Figs 28 and 30 (printed pp 61–63) — Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC
confidence_notes: FM Ch4 is a full US layout sequence with named tools and 8d. CMHC labeled Canadian. Temp toilet Gap. Previous gap-P03-layout-unsourced is superseded for batter boards; toilet remains.
remodel_note: Remodel extras (matching, occupied-site, shoring, demo of an existing house) are not a sequence in CMHC/ORNL/HUD/FM — Gap, do not invent remodel-only methods. Essential Guide is framing-only (opened 2026-08-30; silent on site/layout). B&D Room Additions not used as a P00–P06 sequence.

fastener_schedule.what: secure string line to batter boards
fastener_schedule.pattern: nails in the tops of batter boards (or angle saw cuts)
fastener_schedule.source: FM 5-426 Ch4 LAYOUT tools list: '8d nails are used to secure string line to batter boards.'

labor_notes: FM does not give a headcount. CMHC names a land surveyor as maybe required. No crew count.
layering: Corner stakes first; batter boards 3 or 4 ft outside; lines over the stakes; square; then excavation lines outside the building line as far as required (FM).
CMHC post-excavation boards: Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. Do not mix as a US habit.
code_to_check: Setbacks and side yards: CMHC says check the municipality — Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. Layout follows the permit set. Confirm with AHJ / engineer.
time_money: No dollars. CMHC Ch2: excavation often one day after layout — that duration is P04, not a P03 save.

images.caption: FM 5-426 Fig 4-3: right-angle batter boards 3 or 4 ft outside each corner stake; 2x4 or 4x4 posts, 1x4 or 1x6 boards, 2x2 corner stakes. Tops at top-of-foundation. Saw cuts or nails for building / foundation / footing / excavation lines.
FM 5-426 Fig 4-4: extending lines over corner stakes; 6-8-10 squaring (never start under 6 ft; 12-16-20 on a 50x100). Equal-diagonal method on a rectangle.
FM 5-426 Fig 4-1: laying out a rectangular building from a property/road line. Four corners staked before boards.
CMHC Fig 28: equal diagonals; taut line, saw kerf, plumb bob; 3-4-5 in metres. Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. Do not copy the millimetre 3-4-5 as US habit (US is FM 6-8-10).
CMHC Fig 30: batter boards after excavation, back slope, workspace, footing on undisturbed soil. Canadian / NBC — confirm AHJ; not IRC. US habit is FM boards before the hole so lines survive.

inspector_looks_for: Batter boards outside the hole; lines replaceable in saw kerfs or nails (FM).
Building / foundation / footing / excavation lines marked separately (FM).
Boards level; plumb bob at corners (FM).
do_not_cheap: Batter boards far enough outside that the excavator does not wipe the lines (FM 3 or 4 ft). Hold.
Square before you dig: 6-8-10 never under 6 ft, or equal diagonals (FM). Hold.
Separate marks for building / foundation / footing / excavation (FM layering).
8d nails named to secure string line to batter boards (FM tools list).
smart_save: 6-8-10 vs equal diagonals are both in FM — pick one and prove it, not a product upgrade. No dollars.
Irregular plan: big rectangle first, then small rectangles (FM). Not a new Method.
Late swap: moving the house after the hole is open is a reshoot of layout and maybe a setback problem. Catch vs the survey and the permit set.
